key_insight: A biologically informed dual-branch transformer disentangles baseline cell state from drug-induced regulatory shifts, enabling accurate prediction of nonlinear dose–time transcriptional responses and strong generalization to unseen cellular contexts.
problem_solved: Predicting how cells transcriptionally respond to drugs across varying doses and times is hard because baseline cell identity confounds treatment effects and responses are nonlinear and context-dependent; this model separates those factors to improve accuracy and out-of-distribution generalization.
method: Dual-branch transformer: separate branches encode baseline cell state and drug-induced perturbation, then combine representations to predict post-treatment expression while preserving interpretability.
Biologically informed priors: incorporate pathway/gene-regulatory constraints and domain-specific embeddings to bias the model toward plausible mechanistic shifts.
Dose–time modeling: continuous dose/time embeddings and attention mechanisms capture nonlinear dynamics and interactions across treatment conditions.
impact: Provides a scalable, interpretable framework for modeling perturbation responses that improves OOD generalization and can accelerate in-silico drug screening, mechanistic hypothesis generation, and transfer learning in molecular and single-cell applications.
visual_elements: Architecture schematic showing two parallel transformer branches (cell state vs perturbation) merging into a prediction head with disentanglement arrows.
Dose–time response surface (heatmap or 3D surface) illustrating nonlinear predicted transcriptional trajectories across dose and time.
Embedding visualization (UMAP/t-SNE) showing separation of baseline cell-state embeddings from perturbation embeddings and clustering by response.
Benchmark bar/line chart comparing prediction accuracy and OOD generalization against existing baselines across multiple cell types.
paper_title: Modelling drug-induced cellular perturbation responses with a biologically informed dual-branch transformer
paper_authors: Yue Guo, Hao Zhang, Haitao Hu, Jialu Wu, Ji Cao
